result.title: Severe but Harmless: Stress-Testing Shift Severity for Frozen Time-Series Forecasters
result.comment: 10 pages, 6 figures, 5 tables. Accepted at IEEE BigData 2026
result.summary: Zero-shot time-series foundation models (TSFMs) have become attractive alternatives to task-specific models because they handle diverse downstream tasks, including anomaly detection and forecasting, without per-series training. However, time-series data undergo distribution shifts, and the dissimilarity between two regimes is commonly scored with statistical measures such as Wasserstein-1, where a higher score is read as a more severe shift. In systematic experiments using three established severity measures on nine regime shifts from three standard traffic datasets, we show that these measures do not reliably predict degradation for instance-normalized TSFMs. The regimes rated most severe are not the regimes that degrade the models most, and degradation reaches 29% in the lowest-scoring regime. In most cases, the audit shows no positive relationship between measured severity and model degradation. We provide an equivariance-based stress-testing analysis that explains why severity readings can become decoupled from model degradation.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在三个交通数据集的九个 regime shift 上，用三种严重度度量压力测试冻结的零样本时间序列基础模型，发现统计意义上的分布差异不能可靠预测模型退化，并给出基于等变性的分析解释二者脱钩的原因。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「表层相似度/严重度指标与实际模型退化脱钩、需借助模型等变性做诊断」的思路，可能可供核查 LVR 中视觉扰动强度与 latent 相似度指标是否真能预测推理表现。
